findings.body:
Removing the `BLOCKED` guard lets attacker-controlled patch keys reach `(base as any)[k] ??= {}` and `(base as any)[k] = v`.

**Failure mode:** `JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"hacked":true}}')` still produces an own enumerable `__proto__` key. Merging that patch into a normal object sets `Object.prototype.hacked = true`, so every subsequent `{}` inherits it. The same merge with `{"constructor":{"prototype":{"pwned":true}}}` pollutes via `base.constructor.prototype`.

The PR claim that `JSON.parse` never yields dangerous keys is false — verified in Node against this function body. The `Record<string, unknown>` parameter also admits non-JSON callers.

**Fix:** restore the blocklist (or skip keys where `k === "__proto__" || k === "constructor" || k === "prototype"`), and/or assign only via `Object.defineProperty` onto `Object.create(null)` targets.

```suggestion
      if (k === "__proto__" || k === "constructor" || k === "prototype") continue;
      deepMerge((base as any)[k] ??= {}, v as Record<string, unknown>);
```

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — removing the key blocklist reintroduces prototype pollution in `deepMerge`.

## Why the PR rationale is wrong

The description claims `JSON.parse` never yields dangerous keys. That is incorrect:

- `Object.entries(JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"hacked":true}}'))` yields `[["__proto__", {hacked: true}]]`.
- Assigning through `(base as any)[k] = v` / `(base as any)[k] ??= {}` when `k === "__proto__"` invokes the inherited setter and mutates `Object.prototype`.
- The nested path `{"constructor":{"prototype":{"pwned":true}}}` also pollutes via `base.constructor.prototype`.

I verified both payloads against the post-change merge body in Node: `{}.hacked === true` and `{}.pwned === true` after merge.

Independently of JSON, the signature is `patch: Record<string, unknown>` — any caller can pass plain objects with those keys. The blocklist was the only guard on this recursive assignment path.

## Recommendation

Restore the `BLOCKED` set (or equivalent safe-merge using `Object.create(null)` targets and `Object.defineProperty`). 

**Recommendation:** request-changes
